ageBands.label: ages 6-8
ageBands.note: Picture-led lessons, 10-15 minute sessions, no typing required at the start. An adult usually sits alongside.

ageBands.label: ages 9-11
ageBands.note: The switch to typed code. Sessions stretch to 20-30 minutes and most children can work independently, coming to you only when stuck.
ageBands.worlds: Cosmic Code Station, Algorithm Castle and Game Arcade

ageBands.label: ages 12-14
ageBands.note: Real projects. At this age a child can hold a whole program in their head and will start building things nobody assigned them.
ageBands.worlds: Web Wizard Woods, JavaScript Junction and Function Forge

ageBands.label: ages 15-16
ageBands.note: Depth and portfolio work. Older beginners move fast and should skip the scaffolding entirely - starting at typed code from day one.
ageBands.worlds: AI Island, Data Structures Dojo and Master's Summit

audiences.name: Homeschool families
audiences.desc: A self-paced coding curriculum for homeschool families - no coding knowledge needed to teach it, with records you can keep for your portfolio.
audiences.lead: You don't need to know how to code to teach it. KidVibers is fully self-paced, checks every answer itself, and keeps the records you need for reporting.
points: You are not the teacher here
Each lesson explains its own concept, the child writes real code, and the platform checks the work. A built-in helper gives hints when they're stuck, so progress doesn't stall waiting for you.
Records for your portfolio
Lessons completed, quiz results and printable certificates - dated and per child. If your state asks for evidence of learning, it's already assembled.
One plan, several children
A Family plan covers multiple kids, each on their own track at their own level, so siblings years apart can work at the same table.
Works when the internet doesn't
Lessons cache to the device, so it keeps working on a trip, at a cabin, or on rural internet that comes and goes.

audiences.name: Public libraries
audiences.desc: Drop-in coding sessions for public libraries - no accounts required to start, no ads, and a printable one-pager for your board.
audiences.lead: Run a coding session without pre-registration, staff training, or software installs. It runs in the browser on the machines you already have.
points: Drop-in with a session code
Start a session, give out the code, and children can join and start coding immediately - no account creation at the desk, no email addresses collected on the spot.
Runs on the computers you have
Browser-based, works on older machines and Chromebooks, nothing to install and nothing for IT to approve.
Safe to run unsupervised
No ads, no public gallery, no messaging between users. There is nothing for a child to stumble into while a staff member is helping someone else.
A one-pager for your board
The Trust and Safety page prints as a clean handout covering privacy, safety and data practices - useful for approvals and for parents asking at the desk.

audiences.name: Homeschool co-ops
audiences.desc: Run a coding group across mixed ages without teaching it yourself - one join code, individual tracks, and progress for the whole group in one place.
audiences.lead: Mixed ages are the hard part of a co-op. Decoupling the difficulty from the room solves it.
points: Everyone at their own level
Put each child on their own track. A seven-year-old and a thirteen-year-old can sit together doing completely different work, so the room stays social while the difficulty stays individual.
One code to join
The group leader creates a class code. Children enter it once and they're in - no roster spreadsheet, no per-family setup.
See the whole group at once
Progress for every child in one view, so you know who's flying and who's quietly stuck before it becomes a problem.
The leader doesn't need to code
Your job is timekeeping and unblocking. The lessons teach; the platform checks.

audiences.name: After-school programs
audiences.desc: A coding activity for after-school clubs that works with rotating staff, mixed attendance and kids who arrive at different times.
audiences.lead: After-school is chaotic by nature: kids arrive late, attendance rotates, and staff change week to week. Self-paced tracks absorb all of that.
points: Nobody falls behind by missing a week
Each child resumes exactly where they left off. There is no lesson plan to keep the group synchronised with, so inconsistent attendance stops being a problem.
New staff can run it on day one
There is nothing to prepare and no material to learn ahead of the session. A new staff member can supervise competently the first time.
Short, finishable lessons
Every lesson has a visible end point, so a child who only has twenty minutes still finishes something rather than stopping mid-task.
Safe with light supervision
No ads, no public gallery, no messaging between children.

audiences.name: Teachers and classrooms
audiences.desc: Classroom coding with per-student progress, assignable lessons, school hours enforcement and roster upload.
audiences.lead: Built for a teacher who has twenty-five students at fifteen different levels and one period to work with.
points: Roster upload and class codes
Add students in bulk from a CSV, or hand out a class code and let them join themselves.
Assign lessons with due dates
Set what the class should cover and track who has finished, without forcing everyone through the same lesson on the same day.
School hours
Restrict when students can log in, so the platform is available during your period and not at midnight.
Progress reports you can download
Per-student completion and quiz results, exportable for your own records or for parents evening.

audiences.name: Districts and schools
audiences.desc: District-level coding rollout with per-school management, custom branding, seat management and centralised oversight.
audiences.lead: One account structure covering many classrooms or sites, with the oversight a district actually needs.
points: Many schools under one roof
Manage multiple classrooms or sites centrally, with each school seeing only its own students.
Seat management
Manage the number of student seats you signed up for, and reassign them as cohorts change.
Custom branding
Set your own organisation name and logo so the platform reads as yours to families.
Data and DPA
A dedicated schools privacy page covering what is collected, how it is used, and the data processing terms your procurement team will ask for.
